newsitem.title: USA: Democrat on ethics panel got tape of Gingrich talk.
newsitem.headline: Democrat on ethics panel got tape of Gingrich talk.

text.p: A Florida couple said on Monday they turned over a tape of a controversial telephone conference call between House Speaker Newt Gingrich and his top lieutenants to the senior Democrat on the House of Representatives ethics committee.
The tapes were published in two newspapers two days later, prompting Republican calls for an FBI criminal investigation into the source of the leak.
Confirmation that Representative Jim McDermott of Washington had received the tape turned the last stages of the ethics investigation of Gingrich into a major embarrassment for the Democrats.

"If in fact Congressman McDermott is responsible for the leak, he should resign from Congress immediately," said Representative John Boehner, chairman of the House Republican Conference, who was a participant in the conference call.
The New York Times, in publishing transcripts, said the tapes came from a Democratic member of Congress opposed to Gingrich.

The latest twist in the Gingrich ethics investigation came in Gainesville, Florida, where John and Alice Martin appeared with a lawyer to tell reporters how they picked up the conference call on a police scanner last December while travelling in their car near Jacksonville, Florida.
They recognised some of the voices, used a tape recorder in the car to record the call and gave the tape to McDermott when they were in Washington.
The converation between Gingrich and some of his top lieutenants took place on December 21, the day the ethics committee said Gingrich had violated House rules and he admitted doing so.
When the transcripts were published on Friday Democrats said they showed Gingrich was violating a pledge not to orchestrate his public defence in the ethics case. Republicans deny the accusation.
The latest twist in the Gingrich affair came as the House prepared to vote next Tuesday on a punishment for Gingrich for his ethics violation.
